title: staggered-reservation-slots-and-consistent-utilization-ledger
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds staggered reservation slot allocator and a consistent utilization ledger to improve burst fairness and make autoscaler signals less noisy. Backward compatible; gated behind feature flag by default.
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleet warm pools and burst capacity are noisy under highly concurrent tenant access patterns. Short spikes often cause a flurry of tiny reservations and immediate decommits which both increase churn and make the autoscaler react to spurious signals. This PR introduces two complementary primitives: a staggered reservation slots allocator and a consistent utilization ledger. Goals: 1) Reduce churn by coalescing very short reservations into time-bucketed slots; 2) Produce stable per-tenant and per-pool utilization metrics that the autoscaler and chargeback systems can depend on; 3) Maintain predictable throughput guarantees while preserving burst headroom for latency-sensitive tenants. Changes (summary): - pkg/autoscaler/staggered_slots.go: new allocator that assigns short-lived reservations into staggered slots, with occupancy windows and eviction grace; includes unit-tested slot reclamation heuristics. - pkg/orchestrator/utilization_ledger.go: ledger implementation that records slot ownership and normalized utilization contributions, exposing TTL-backed ledger entries so disconnects don't lose accounting. - controllers/reservation_controller.go: adapter logic to use staggered slots for requests below the SHORT_RESERVE_MS threshold and fallback to exact reservations otherwise. - api/v1/reservations.proto: added fields for reserve_slot_id and ledger_window to the ReserveResponse/ReserveRequest contracts (backwards compatible: new fields are optional). - charts/redwood-helm/values.yaml: new feature flag enableStaggeredSlots (off by default) and telemetry sampling knobs. - docs/ops/reservations.md: operational guide for enabling the feature, expected behavior, and debug tips. - tests/unit/staggered_slots_test.go, tests/integration/ledger_end2end_test.go: new test harness covering race conditions and cluster recovery scenarios. Compatibility and rollout: The feature is behind the enableStaggeredSlots feature flag which defaults to false for existing deployments. The ledger exposes a short retention window (default 10m) and falls back to previous metrics when disabled. We added a migration path that will run in parallel (no destructive database migration). Observability: New metrics: redwood_reservation_slot_allocations_total, redwood_slot_utilization_p50/p95, redwood_ledger_entries_active, redwood_reservation_slot_evictions_total. Added traces for slot allocation decisions to the existing reservations span. Backfill plan: once feature is on for canary clusters, we'll run load profiles from benchmark-lab against predictable synthetic tenants to tune slot window and eviction thresholds. Checklist: - [x] Add allocator and ledger implementations - [x] API additions (optional fields) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Helm values + feature flag - [x] Documentation - [x] Perf benchmarks and telemetry hooks Security review: No sensitive data changes, ledger entries are identifiers only. KMS/HSM or audit logging not affected. Runtime implications: Small memory increase for in-memory ledger state in each controller (default window keeps ~N entries per active tenant). Autoscaler integration: Autoscaler now ingests redwood_slot_utilization_* metrics and uses a new smoothing factor to prevent over-reacting to transient slot churn. See ENG-1128 for design notes.
